extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of art history, aesthetics, and literary criticism; creative writers interested in Hellenic aesthetic principles
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting or applying criteria for producing and judging art (especially sculpture, painting, poetry) according to Pater's account of Hellenic aesthetic principles and their implications for mediums, form, and temperament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine Enthusiasm as a Critical Virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Enthusiasm ... was the secret of his divinatory power over the Hellenic world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A true affinity for an artistic tradition is not mere learned consultation but a lived enthusiasm that re-enforces intellectual perception with near-physical excitement. Anti-pattern: dry, purely scholarly acquaintance ('learned men who might be consulted like books') that lacks personal, temperamental investment and thus fails to 'make himself a pagan' for penetrating antiquity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affinity Must Be Temperamental, Not Only Intellectual
rubrics_metrics.description: That his affinity with Hellenism was not merely intellectual, that the subtler threads of temperament were inwoven in it, is proved by his romantic, fervent friendships with young men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical sympathy should be rooted in temperament and embodied instincts (including personal taste and friendships) rather than solely in abstract study. Scoring note: weight emotional/temperamental engagement positively when assessing authenticity of aesthetic appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial Sensibility Toward Male and Female Beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who are observant of beauty only in women, and are moved little or not at all by the beauty of men, seldom have an impartial, vital, inborn instinct for beauty in art. To such persons the beauty of Greek art will ever seem wanting, because its supreme beauty is rather male than female.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A critic or maker should cultivate an impartial and broad sensibility for beauty across sexes; a narrowly gendered taste limits appreciation of Greek art's ideals. Anti-pattern: selective appreciation that privileges only female beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture Awakens the Taste for Artistic Beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: The beauty of art ... must be awakened and repaired by culture. Now, as the spirit of culture is much more ardent in youth than in manhood, the instinct ... must be exercised and directed to what is beautiful, before that age is reached ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taste for art is not purely natural; it requires cultivation from an early age. Practical implication: educational formation and continuous exposure are criteria for genuine taste. Scoring/guidance: reward works and critics that show evidence of cultivated, historically-informed taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art Should Saturate Form with Motive (Not Mere Symbolism)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Venus of Melos ... is in no sense a symbol, a suggestion of anything beyond its own victorious fairness. The mind begins and ends with the finite image, yet loses no part of the spiritual motive. That motive ... saturates and is identical with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ideal is an artwork whose form and motive are identical—meaning and sensuous form inseparable. Anti-patterns: over-symbolic works where form only hints at ideas beyond itself (as with many medieval or oriental works), leaving the matter inadequately embodied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match Medium to Imaginative Motive
rubrics_metrics.description: Different attitudes of the imagination have a native affinity with different types of sensuous form ... architecture ... sculpture ... painting, music, and poetry ... Sculpture ... deals immediately with man, while ... poetry and painting ... are the special arts of the romantic and modern ages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the chosen medium suits the motive: use architecture for grand/spatial concerns, sculpture for human form and type, poetry/painting/music for inward, complex, situational expression. Anti-pattern: forcing a motive into an ill-suited medium (e.g., treating a delicately psychological situation as monumental sculpture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sculpture: Purge the Accidental to Reveal Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Sculpture ... has to choose from a select number of types intrinsically interesting ... It effects not by accumulation of detail, but by abstracting from it. All that is accidental, all that distracts the simple effect ... it gradually purges away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sculptural (or sculpturally-inspired) works should abstract away incidental detail and emphasize broad, incisive lines of character-type. Scoring note: reward restraint and abstraction that reveal an archetypal humanity rather than cluttered specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heiterkeit and Allgemeinheit — Blitheness and Generality
rubrics_metrics.description: Heiterkeit--blitheness or repose, and Allgemeinheit--generality or breadth, are, then, the supreme characteristics of the Hellenic ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The highest aesthetic value lies in a composed, reposeful tone and a breadth that conveys universality. Evaluate works for an air of serene clarity and a sense of humanity generalized into ideal types rather than idiosyncratic extremes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality Arises from Minute, Severe, Renewed Culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Hellenic breadth and generality come of a culture minute, severe, constantly renewed, rectifying and concentrating its impressions into certain pregnant types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generality is not laziness: it is the product of disciplined, painstaking cultural practice. Assess whether 'broad' effects are founded on careful study, correction, and refinement rather than on careless simplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit Passion to Avoid Transience and Grotesque Excess
rubrics_metrics.description: Works of art produced under this law ... keep passion always below that degree of intensity at which it must necessarily be transitory ... All such instances may be ranged under the grotesque; and the Hellenic ideal has nothing in common with the grotesque.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer controlled expression of feeling that preserves lasting, ideal quality; penalize works that amplify one emotion to an excessive, single-note intensity (grotesque/overwrought).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Ideal Requires Harmonious Union of Body and Mind
rubrics_metrics.description: This ideal art ... was joined, by some supreme good luck, to the perfect animal nature of the Greeks. Here are the two conditions of an artistic ideal ... the finer aspects of nature, the finer ... of the human form, and modelling of the dainty framework of the human countenance:--these are the good luck of the Greek when he enters upon life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic judgments should account for the interplay between sensual, bodily qualities and intellectual/cultural refinement. Works that achieve an ideal harmonize physical form with reflective thought rather than privileging one to the detriment of the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical Cultivation as Part of Aesthetic Formation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Greek system of gymnastics originated as part of a religious ritual. The worshipper was to recommend himself to the gods by becoming fleet and fair, white and red ... The beauty of the palaestra, and the beauty of the artist's studio, reacted on each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the social and bodily cultivation that underlies standards of beauty; aesthetic evaluation can legitimately include attention to embodied practices and socio-cultural rituals that shape form. Anti-pattern: judging works in isolation from the bodily and civic contexts that produced their aesthetic ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry and Painting: Situation over Character; Use of Detail and Atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: In poetry and painting, the situation predominates over the character ... To realise this situation ... the artist has to employ the most cunning detail, to complicate and refine upon thought and passion a thousand-fold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For narrative/lyric arts, value the construction of an arresting situation and skillful atmospheric detail that elevates characters (even trivial ones) into ideal moments. Scoring note: award the artful orchestration of indirect expression, foreground/background, and subtle allusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Overburdening Form with Inexpressible Thought
rubrics_metrics.description: In some strange halo ... Angelico's fresco ... cannot be said ... to throw into a sensible form our highest thoughts ... Such forms of art ... are inadequate to the matter they clothe; they remain ever below its level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of seeking to represent ideas that a medium cannot sensibly embody; if thought outruns sensible form, the result will feel inadequate. Anti-pattern: creating overcharged symbolic forms (many-headed gods, overwrought allegory) that hint at inexpressible ideas without satisfying embodiment.
